                    SEngland's Harry Kane celebrates after the match. Photo: Action Images via Reuters
                                      </p></div><div id="content-body-71544740" class="articlebodycontent col-xl-9 col-lg-12 col-md-12 col-sm-12 col-12"><div class="schemaDiv" id="schemaDiv" itemprop="articleBody"><p >Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored twice apiece as England demolished Luka Modric's Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka on Saturday, but Spain stayed three points clear at ​the top of their Nations League group with a 3-1 victory over the Czech Republic.</p><p >Jude Bellingham scored ‌once and provided three assists for England, with Anthony Gordon and substitute ​Morgan Rogers also on target in a performance captain Kane described as "unbelievable".</p><p >England ⁠are second in League A, Group Three with six points from three matches, behind Spain on nine. Croatia have three points and the Czechs remain pointless.</p><p >"Unbelievable from start to finish," Kane told ITV. "We ‌spoke a lot about having a 90-minute game from start to finish, being completely dominant with the ball and without the ball. That was it ‌right there."</p><p >Kane took his international tally to 89 goals in 124 appearances, moving ‌within ⁠one cap of Peter Shilton's England record.</p><p >Asked about potentially drawing level with Shilton ⁠against the Czech Republic on Tuesday, Kane said: "Would be nice. That is why he (manager Thomas Tuchel) takes me off, to save me for the next one!"</p><p >England went ahead after little more than seven minutes when Josko ​Gvardiol lost possession and Bellingham released ‌Kane, who slipped between two defenders and fired home.</p><p >Bellingham doubled the lead in the 21st minute after Gordon turned Saka's cross back across goal. Gordon added the third in the 39th, meeting Jarell Quansah's cross with a first-time finish.</p><p >Mateo Kovacic squandered a ‌close-range chance before Bellingham crossed for an unmarked Saka to score a minute ​before halftime.</p><p >Elliot Anderson supplied Kane's second goal with a low cross in the 53rd minute, before Josip Stanisic's misplaced pass across his own box ⁠gifted Saka another goal in the 68th.</p><p >Bellingham released Rogers to complete the rout three minutes from time.</p><p >"They couldn't live with our pace, with our runs," Kane said.</p><p >SPAIN KEEP WINNING</p><p >World and European ‌champions Spain maintained their perfect start in Oviedo despite coach Luis de la Fuente making nine changes to the side that beat Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday.</p><p >Lamine Yamal opened the scoring in the sixth minute, curling a stunning left-footed shot into the top corner from the edge of the box.</p><p >After Spain squandered several opportunities, captain Rodri doubled their advantage by converting a rebound inside the area, his first international goal in more than two years.</p><p >Jiri ‌Slama gave the visitors hope in the 69th minute, finishing a swift counter-attack with an angled shot just ​inside David Raya's right post.</p><p >Their chances of an equaliser faded when Ladislav Krejci received a second booking in the 85th minute for holding back ⁠an opponent to stop a counter-attack.</p><p >Mikel Merino then sealed Spain's victory, finishing first time from inside ⁠the box following another quick break.</p><p >In League B, Scotland won 2-0 at North Macedonia through goals from Kieron Bowie and John McGinn before Scott McKenna was ‌sent off in the 83rd minute.</p><p >Switzerland came from behind to beat Slovenia 2-1 in Luzern, with an Erik Janza own goal and Dan Ndoye's strike overturning Zan Vipotnik's ​opener.
